'''Tanya Mary Monro''' {{postnominals|country=AUS|AC}} (born 1973)<ref name=FAA>[http://science.org.au/awards/awardees/2012awards.html 2012 Pawsey Medal for outstanding research in physics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130205200410/http://www.science.org.au/awards/awardees/2012awards.html |date=5 February 2013 }}, science.org.au</ref><ref name=RiAus>[http://riaus.org.au/people/tanya-monro/ Prof. Tanya Monro] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110091200/http://riaus.org.au/people/tanya-monro/ |date=10 January 2017 }}, Royal Institution of Australia, riaus.org.au</ref> is an Australian physicist known for her work in [[photonics]]. She has been Australia's [[Chief Defence Scientist]] since 8 March 2019. Prior to that, she was the Deputy Vice Chancellor, Research and Innovation (DVCR&I) at the [[University of South Australia]]. She was awarded the [[Australian Research Council|ARC]] [[Georgina Sweet Australian Laureate Fellowship]] in 2013. She was the inaugural director of the Institute for Photonics & Advanced Sensing (IPAS)<ref name=IPAS/> (now known as the School of Physical Sciences). Monro has remained an adjunct professor of physics at the University of Adelaide following her departure from the institution. In 2020, she was awarded the title of Emeritus Professor at the [[University of South Australia]].

Her previous board roles have included membership of the Australian Prime Minister's Commonwealth Science Council,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/academy-newsletter/australian-academy-science-newsletter-98/new-council-advise-pm-science|title=New council to advise PM on science {{!}} Australian Academy of Science|website=www.science.org.au|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> the [[Economic Development Board (South Australia)|South Australian Economic Development Board]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.statedevelopment.sa.gov.au/news-releases/all-news-updates/economic-development-board-renewed-with-new-agenda|title=Economic Development Board renewed with new agenda|website=www.statedevelopment.sa.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20|archive-date=26 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326000842/https://statedevelopment.sa.gov.au/news-releases/all-news-updates/economic-development-board-renewed-with-new-agenda|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[Defence SA]] board.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.premier.sa.gov.au/index.php/martin-hamilton-smith-news-releases/1110-minister-welcomes-new-defencesa-advisory-board-members|title=Minister welcomes new DefenceSA Advisory Board members - Jay Weatherill, Premier of South Australia|website=www.premier.sa.gov.au|language=en-gb|access-date=2017-04-20|archive-date=20 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170420234615/http://www.premier.sa.gov.au/index.php/martin-hamilton-smith-news-releases/1110-minister-welcomes-new-defencesa-advisory-board-members|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
Monro was awarded a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree with first-class honours in 1995<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sydney.edu.au/science/physics/about/profiles/monro.shtml|title=Student & Graduate profiles|last=|first=|date=27 February 2013|website=The University of Sydney|access-date=2018-01-21}}</ref> followed by a [[PhD]] in 1998 from the [[University of Sydney]] for research on [[waveguide]]s. Monro credits a teacher at [[SCEGGS Darlinghurst|Sydney Church of England Girls Grammar]] with inspiring her interest in physics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://cosmosmagazine.com/science/physics/tanya-monros-brilliant-career/|title=Tanya Monro's brilliant career {{!}} Cosmos|website=cosmosmagazine.com|date=6 April 2015 |language=en|access-date=2018-01-21}}</ref>

==Career and research==
From 1998 to 2004, Monro was a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] at the Optoelectronics Research Centre (ORC) at the [[University of Southampton]].<ref name=royalsoc/> She joined the University of Adelaide in 2005 as inaugural chair of photonics and Director of the Centre of Expertise in Photonics (CoEP) within the School of Chemistry & Physics in partnership with DSTO. Since that time and while at the University of Adelaide she has been: ARC Federation Fellow; Director of the Institute for Photonics & Advanced Sensing (IPAS)<ref name=IPAS>[http://www.adelaide.edu.au/ipas/ Institute for Photonics & Advanced Sensing], University of Adelaide</ref> and the  Director of the ARC Centre of Excellence in Nanoscale Biophotonics at the University of Adelaide. From 2014 to 2019  she was the Deputy Vice Chancellor and Vice President, Research and Innovation at the University of South Australia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.unisa.edu.au/media-centre/releases/top-australian-scientist-to-lead-research-at-unisa/|title=Top Australian scientist to lead research at UniSA|last=UniSA|website=www.unisa.edu.au|language=en-AU|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref>

=== Chief Defence Scientist (2019–present) ===

Monro was announced as Australia's next Chief Defence Scientist on 24 January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Chief Defence Scientist announced |url=https://www.dst.defence.gov.au/news-media/media-releases/new-chief-defence-scientist-announced |website=Defence Science and Technology Group |date=24 January 2019 |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref> Monro took up the role of [[Chief Defence Scientist]] in March 2019, the first woman in this position.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dst.defence.gov.au/news/2019/01/24/new-chief-defence-scientist-announced |title=New Chief Defence Scientist announced |date=24 January 2019 |publisher=[[Defence Science and Technology Group]] |access-date=25 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/academy-fellow-appointed-chief-defence-scientist|title=Academy Fellow appointed Chief Defence Scientist |publisher=Australian Academy of Science |website=www.science.org.au|access-date=25 January 2019}}</ref>
In this role, she heads the Defence Science and Technology Group and serves as Defence's Capability Manager for Innovation, Science and Technology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chief Defence Scientist |url=https://www.defence.gov.au/about/who-we-are/leaders/chief-defence-scientist |website=Department of Defence |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref>

During her tenure, Defence released and implemented the mission-directed S&T framework known as ''More, together: Defence Science and Technology Strategy 2030'', which established the Science, Technology and Research (STaR) Shots to focus effort on leap-ahead capabilities, including Remote Undersea Surveillance and Quantum-Assured Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Science, Technology and Research (STaR) Shots – overview |url=https://www.dst.defence.gov.au/sites/default/files/basic_pages/documents/Booklet%20-%20STaR%20Shots.pdf |website=Department of Defence |date=August 2020 |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Remote Undersea Surveillance (STaR Shot) |url=https://www.dst.defence.gov.au/strategy/star-shots/remote-undersea-surveillance |website=Department of Defence |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Quantum-Assured PNT (STaR Shot) |url=https://www.dst.defence.gov.au/strategy/star-shots/quantum-assured-pnt |website=Department of Defence |access-date=12 October 2025}}</ref>

== Publications ==
{{Scholia}}Monro has published a few book chapters, and is named on 275 papers (Monro is first and/or sole author in only 40 of these papers), including refereed journal articles and conference papers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholia.toolforge.org/author/Q7684027|title=Tanya Monro Scholia|website=scholia.toolforge.org|language=en|access-date=2024-05-26}}</ref> These have led to more than 21000 citations<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com.au/citations?user=OZRXWZoAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Tanya Monro - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com.au|access-date=2023-08-11}}</ref> in journals and refereed conference proceedings. Monro has also registered a number of patent families,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/tanya-monro|title=Tanya Monro Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com|language=en|access-date=2018-01-21}}</ref> although not one of these patent families have resulted in any commercial applications or uses – as is typical of blue sky researchers.

== Honours and awards ==
*1998: The [[Bragg Gold Medal]] for Excellence in Physics for the best PhD thesis by a student from an Australian university<ref name=FF08Bio>[http://www.arc.gov.au/pdf/FedFellows_bios08.pdf Professor Tanya Monro] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120707102741/http://arc.gov.au/pdf/FedFellows_bios08.pdf |date=7 July 2012 }}, Biographies of 2008 round of Federation Fellows, [[Australian Research Council]]</ref>
*2006: Bright Spark Award (for Australia's Top 10 Scientific Minds under 45 – Cosmos Magazine)<ref name=FF08Bio/>
*2012: [[Pawsey Medal]]<ref>The [[Pawsey Medal]] is awarded annually by the [[Australian Academy of Science]] to recognise outstanding research in the field of physics by an Australian scientist under the age of 40. [http://science.org.au/news/media/6december11-2.html 2012 Early-career research awards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130206092049/http://www.science.org.au/news/media/6december11-2.html |date=6 February 2013 }}, 2012 Academy awards for scientific excellence announced, Media release, 6 December 2011, Australian Academy of Science</ref> 
*2015: [[Eureka Prizes|Eureka Prize]] for Excellence in Interdisciplinary Scientific Research<ref>{{cite web|url=https://australian.museum/about/organisation/media-centre/2015-eureka-interdisciplinary-scientific-research|title=2015 University of New South Wales Eureka Prize for Excellence in Interdisciplinary Scientific Research|website=australian.museum|access-date=2022-08-11}}</ref>
*2019: South Australian award winner of The Australian Awards for Excellence in Women's Leadership.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wla.edu.au/award-winners/professor-tanya-monro|title=The Awards for Excellence in Women's Leadership - Tanya Monro|website=www.wla.edu.au|access-date=2022-08-11}}</ref>
*2020: Awarded the title of Emeritus Professor at the [[University of South Australia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unisa.edu.au/about-unisa/Honorary-Doctorates/past-award-winners/#emeritus-professor|title=Past Honorary Award recipients|website=www.unisa.edu.au|access-date=2022-08-11}}</ref>
*2022: Appointed [[Companion of the Order of Australia]] in the [[2022 Queen's Birthday Honours (Australia)|2022 Queen's Birthday Honours]] for "eminent service to scientific and technological development, to research and innovation, to tertiary education, particularly in the field of photonics, and to professional organisations".<ref name="SMH QB2022">{{cite news |title=Queen's Birthday 2022 Honours - the full list |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/queen-s-birthday-2022-honours-the-full-list-20220609-p5askg.html |access-date=12 June 2022 |work=Sydney Morning Herald |agency=Nine Entertainment Co. |date=12 June 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Monro was raised in the Sydney suburb of [[Bankstown]]. She is an alumna of the [[National Youth Science Forum]], a youth camp at the Australian National University students wishing to pursue a career in science. She married David in 1995. They moved to England in 1998. They have three sons, the first born in 2003, followed by twin boys born in 2006.<ref>Abbie Thomas (25 January 2012) [https://www.abc.net.au/science/articles/2012/01/25/3415329.htm "A fetish for photons"], ABC Science</ref> Monro is a science fiction fan, and played cello in the [[Burnside Symphony Orchestra]] in Adelaide.<ref name=":0" />
